title: Group behaviour and interpersonal relationships
summary: How groups form, compete and cooperate, and how attraction, communication and chemical messengers affect close relationships.

keyterms.definition: Sherif: competition between groups for limited resources produces hostility.
A goal that groups can only reach by working together, reducing conflict.
Allport (1954): prejudice can be reduced by contact between groups under certain conditions, e.g. equal status.
Aronson: students in mixed groups each hold part of the material, so they must cooperate.
Physical nearness, which increases the chance of forming relationships.
Shared attitudes, values and characteristics, which increase attraction.
A hormone and neurotransmitter linked to bonding and trust.
Gottman: criticism, contempt, defensiveness and stonewalling, which predict relationship breakdown.
Explaining the cause of someone's behaviour, e.g. as due to their character or the situation.

questions.prompt: In Sherif et al.'s Robbers Cave study, what increased hostility between the Eagles and the Rattlers?
options: Competitive tournaments with prizes for the winners
questions.explanation: Competition for limited resources produced hostility, supporting realistic conflict theory.

questions.prompt: What reduced conflict between the groups in Robbers Cave?
options: Superordinate goals, like fixing the water supply together
questions.explanation: Cooperation on shared goals reduced hostility.

questions.statement: Allport's contact hypothesis says any contact between groups automatically reduces prejudice.
questions.explanation: Contact works under conditions such as equal status, shared goals, cooperation and institutional support.

questions.statement: The jigsaw classroom applies cooperative interdependence to reduce prejudice among students.
questions.explanation: Each student's piece is needed, so students must rely on each other.

questions.text: A goal that requires two groups to cooperate is a ___ goal.
questions.explanation: Sherif used these to reduce conflict.

questions.text: Sherif's explanation of group hostility is called realistic ___ theory.
questions.explanation: It focuses on competition for real resources.

questions.prompt: Match each concept to its key study or researcher.
questions.explanation: SIT suggests categorization alone can cause bias, while realistic conflict stresses competition.

questions.prompt: A limitation of the Robbers Cave study is that:
options: It used a large random sample of adults
Participants were a small group of similar boys, limiting generalization
It took place in a lab
It had no measures of behaviour
questions.explanation: All were white, middle-class boys of about 11–12 at a summer camp.

questions.prompt: Which situation best meets the conditions of the contact hypothesis?
options: A manager supervising workers from another group
Mixed teams of equal status working on a shared project supported by the school
Brief contact in a crowded street
questions.explanation: Equal status, cooperation, common goals and support are key.

questions.prompt: Order the phases of the Robbers Cave study.
questions.explanation: Hostility appeared during competition and fell with cooperation.

questions.prompt: Festinger, Schachter and Back (1950) studied friendships in student housing. Friendships were most common between:
options: People living close to each other
questions.explanation: Proximity increased interaction and friendship.

questions.prompt: Scheele et al. (2012) gave men oxytocin before meeting an attractive woman. Men in monogamous relationships:
options: Kept a greater distance from her
questions.explanation: Single men were not affected, suggesting oxytocin may help maintain existing bonds.

questions.statement: Gottman found contempt was one of the strongest predictors of divorce.
questions.explanation: Contempt is one of the four horsemen, often seen as the most damaging.

questions.statement: Bradbury and Fincham (1990) found that distressed couples tend to explain a partner's positive behaviour as due to their stable character.
questions.explanation: Distressed couples tended to attribute positive behaviour to situations and negative behaviour to the partner's character.

questions.text: Gottman's four horsemen are criticism, contempt, defensiveness and ___.
questions.explanation: Stonewalling means withdrawing from interaction.

questions.text: Explaining a partner's behaviour in terms of personality or situation is making an ___.
questions.explanation: Maladaptive attributions can maintain conflict.

questions.prompt: Match each factor to a relationship study.
questions.explanation: Relationships involve biological, cognitive and sociocultural factors.

questions.prompt: Which strategy would a Gottman-based therapist encourage?
options: Expressing complaints gently without blame and showing appreciation
Using contempt to make a point
questions.explanation: Replacing the four horsemen with gentle start-ups and appreciation is linked to stable relationships.

questions.prompt: Why might research on similarity and attraction be culturally limited?
options: Many studies use Western students, and in some cultures families play a major role in partner choice
questions.explanation: Arranged or family-influenced marriages may involve different criteria.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a typical Gottman-style intervention.
items: Identify the four horsemen in their communication
questions.explanation: Interventions target observable communication.
